title: São Paulo vs Santos: 21st‑round classic and Coutinho’s debut
seoTitle: São Paulo vs Santos – 21st round classic, Coutinho debut
subtitle: Match at Morumbi pits a positional battle and Philippe Coutinho’s return to the field
excerpt: São Paulo and Santos face off this Friday, Oct 2, at 8 p.m. at Morumbi in the 21st round of the Brasileirão.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
São Paulo and Santos will take the field this Friday, October 2, at 8 p.m. (Brasília time) at Morumbi Stadium for the 21st round of the Brazilian Championship. The classic draws attention because of Philippe Coutinho’s much‑anticipated debut and the fight for table positions that could bring one of the clubs closer to a pre‑Libertadores spot.

Why the classic is in the spotlight

Beyond the historic rivalry, the match marks Philippe Coutinho’s return to action. The midfielder, who joined Santos after a seven‑month spell without playing and was convinced by Neymar to resume his career, is contracted until December and will have the chance to feature in the final 11 games of the Brasileirão, helping the side in the battle for a Copa Libertadores berth.

Date, time and broadcast

The clash will be broadcast live on the pay‑TV channels Sportv and Premiere. Real‑time coverage can be followed on the Band.com.br website, and an audio stream is available on Rádio Bandeirantes.

Line‑ups and absences

For São Paulo, coach Dorival Júnior will be without forward Calleri (suspended) and defender Domingos Duarte (anterior cruciate ligament rupture). Young Ryan Francisco has a chance to start, while Bobadilla could return to midfield. Santos, led by Cuca, is expected to line up Arthur, Rodinei, Everton Cebolinha and the other announced starters, with Neymar, Gabriel Brazão, Luan Peres and Gabriel Bontempo unavailable due to medical or suspension issues.

Implications for the Libertadores table

Santos, with 38 points in 8th place, is enjoying a six‑game unbeaten run and is chasing a fifth consecutive win – a feat not seen since Jorge Sampaoli’s campaign. A victory could bring them even closer to the pre‑Libertadores race, while São Paulo, sitting 11th with 36 points, will look to use home advantage to climb the standings.

Emotional tribute to the club

Santos will take the field wearing a custom patch in honor of supporter Naty Potira, who recently passed away, reinforcing the Outubro Rosa campaign. The gesture highlights the solidarity between fans and the club around the cause of early detection of cervical cancer.

With information from ge, Esporte, R7 Esportes.
